title: How to Build a Big Business With a Small Brand in 2026
author: Sharran Srivatsaa
summary: Srivatsaa builds his argument on a supply-and-demand reading of social platforms: human attention is bounded by people multiplied by time, while the supply of passable content is no longer bounded by anything now that AI has collapsed the cost of producing it. He works the arithmetic to show that a platform can grow its total impressions while the attention available to any single competitive piece falls sharply, an effect he names The Great Impression Deflation. The practical consequence is that copying whatever is currently winning has a shrinking half-life, because the same tools that let a creator spot an outlier let everyone else spot it at the same speed. His answer has two parts. The first is Qualume, quality multiplied by volume, which he defines not as posting more but as producing at your maximum volume without dropping below your own quality threshold. The second, and the one he treats as the durable advantage, is street cred: an achievement outside the content pipeline that could regenerate your reputation if the reputation were taken away, and that is specific to the domain you are claiming. This reframes Gary Vaynerchuk's document-don't-create advice as a credibility strategy rather than a production shortcut, and it inverts the old creator advantage, since AI can now hand distribution skill to an accomplished operator far more easily than it can hand accomplishment to a skilled distributor.
points: The core diagnosis is that total impressions can rise while attention per competitive piece collapses, which Srivatsaa illustrates with a worked example showing a 78 percent decline.
He argues that swiping proven winners is a decaying edge because AI shortens the gap between spotting an outlier and shipping a copy of it.
Qualume is defined as maximum volume at your own quality threshold, not maximum volume, since collapsing quality devalues every additional shot.
His credibility test is whether an achievement could regenerate a reputation from scratch, and he insists that street cred does not transfer across domains.
The closing asymmetry is that AI can give an accomplished person creator skills more readily than it can give a creator real accomplishments.
quotes: So this means demand is constrained, but supply is not. And now with AI, the gap between supply and demand is becoming much bigger.
So total attention grew by 10%, but the available attention per competitive piece fell from 10,000 to 2,200. This is a 78% decline.
Creators have always copied winners, but now AI compresses the cycle between identifying an outlier and posting it.
This is why Qualume isn’t to “post as much as possible.” It’s simply: your maximum volume at your quality threshold.
And so this is why the achievement has to be capable of recreating the specific reputation being claimed.
If the camera disappeared tomorrow, would you still be doing the thing you are making content about?
It can give accomplished people creator capabilities much faster than it can give creators accomplishment.

The bottom line is that AI can help everyone make more content. But it can’t give them credibility. And when anyone can look credible, the value of actually being credible becomes the new currency of attention.
